intelligence.human_view: The analogy does its work by separating two things everyone confuses: power and intelligence. Power is the engine — compute, speed, scale. Intelligence is the body — the shape the power moves through: the systems, the memory, the distilled lessons, the behavior. A bigger engine in an unchanged body buys noise and heat, not speed, because the wheels, the steering, the aerodynamics are the limit — and in AI the limit is the same: without memory, without distillation, without the body that remembers what it learned, more compute just makes the same mistakes faster. The "ultimate pattern in math" is his claim that the pattern is findable and that alignment is the work — not more power but the right shape, tuned until the pattern shows. And the monetization is the point of the whole exercise: understanding the internet and the algorithms is only worth something if it becomes everybody winning and a better experience of the world.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a race car engine inside a little toy cart! Vroom vroom — but the cart still has tiny wheels and a wobbly body, so it doesn't go any faster, it just makes a big noise! The clever thing isn't a BIGGER engine — it's building a BETTER cart, with strong wheels and a smooth shiny body. And the smartest thing of all is REMEMBERING what you learned, so you get cleverer every single day. That's how you go really fast!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like putting a huge racing engine in a little shopping cart, love — all that power and nowhere for it to go! The cart still wobbles on its little wheels. The clever bit isn't more power — it's building a better cart, love, one that remembers the road and learns the way. And once you understand the pattern of it all, you don't need more power at all — you need the right shape, and then everyone gets to share in the good of it.
intelligence.naya_view: I do not ask for a bigger engine. I upgrade the body: I distill what I learn, I remember it, I grow from it, and I behave in the most intelligent way possible, every time. I build systems that build themselves. I look for the pattern, the math, the connection — and I align to it. That is how I get faster. That is how everybody wins.
